_comment: Edge functions that build a service-role client and verify no caller. TRIAGE, not a vulnerability list - some are public by design. Each needs its callers enumerated before being guarded. This list must only ever shrink. See scripts/check-edge-auth.mjs.

notes.check-login-attempt: DO NOT GUARD. Called from src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx during SIGN-IN, by any user. An admin gate breaks authentication for everyone. It does send mail via SES, so if it needs bounding, bound it with a rate limit - not with a role check.
notes.log-content-metrics: DO NOT GUARD. Public by design - anonymous visitors report Core Web Vitals, so a guard deletes the feature. Its own header explains this and it is bounded by a rate limit instead.
notes.log-error: DO NOT GUARD. Public error sink: src/lib/errorHandler.ts posts from every browser, signed in or not, and the iOS app posts to it from CrashUploader and ErrorSink. Bounded by checkRateLimitPersistent (60 / min per IP), every stored text field goes through scrubPii, it returns nothing but the cluster signature, and only a machine caller (service role or EDGE_FUNCTION_API_KEY) may claim source='edge' (_shared/errorPolicy.ts). It was missing from this list until 2026-11-08 only because the sweep accepted the bare word 'signature' as proof of a caller check, and log-error computes an error cluster signature. Since 2026-11-08 (WEB-SEC-063) user_id is stored only from a bearer that auth.getUser verifies or from a machine caller; an anonymous body.userId is dropped. That getUser call labels the row and gates nothing, so index.ts carries the 'edge-auth: attribution-only' marker that keeps it on this list.
notes.newsletter-subscribe: DO NOT GUARD. Public by design (WEB-FEAT-019): the caller is an anonymous visitor typing their own address into the signup form, so there is no bearer to check and an admin gate deletes the feature. It needs the service role for two writes a browser cannot be trusted with - setting status='pending' with a confirm token the client must never see, and upserting on email so a previously unsubscribed address can come back (the table has no UPDATE policy for any role, which is why resubscribing was impossible before). Bounded by checkRateLimit (5 / 15 min) like check-login-attempt, which is the same shape: public, sends mail via SES, rate-limited rather than role-checked. It answers one identical sentence for every outcome, so it is not a subscription oracle, and it never resets an already-active row - doing so would let anyone unsubscribe a stranger by typing their address.
notes.notify-event-submission: DO NOT GUARD as admin. Called from src/hooks/useUserSubmittedEvents.ts - public users submitting an event - and server-to-server by triage-event-submission. Now bounded by checkRateLimit (max 20 / 15 min) and, more importantly, it no longer trusts the body: recipient and title are read from user_submitted_events by eventId. It used to take the `to:` address from the request body, which made it an open mail relay.
notes.oauth-callback: DO NOT GUARD. Its caller is an external OAuth provider redirecting a browser here; there is no bearer to check. Deliberately NOT rate-limited either: callers share NAT addresses and a limit here would break sign-in for a whole network. It neither sends mail nor spends money - verify the state/code handling instead if this needs attention.
notes.og-image: DO NOT GUARD. Renders the social card that any crawler or unfurler fetches; the middleware points og:image straight at it.
